podcast.title: Ministry's Outtakes Project
podcast.body: 1000 Homo DJs served as a "goofy side project" initiated by Al Jourgensen of Ministry to release material, specifically Ministry outtakes, while maintaining a clear separation from the main band. The project involved all contributing members adopting fake names for their credits, including Jourgensen (Lux/Buck Satan), Paul Barker (Pan/Officer Aggro), and William Rieflin (We Willy Riefer), and famously included uncredited vocals from Trent Reznor. "He started a goofy side project called 1000 Home Old DJs as a way of releasing some ministry outtakes while keeping things separate from his main band."

xref.title: Legal Battle with TVT Records
xref.body: Trent Reznor endured a significant and "protracted legal battle" with TVT Records after label head Steve Gottlieb expressed disdain for Nine Inch Nails' music, reportedly calling Pretty Hate Machine "an abortion," despite expecting a Depeche Mode-like electronic act. This dispute legally prevented Reznor from recording any music under his name or as Nine Inch Nails, leading him to participate uncredited in side projects like 1000 Homo DJs. "What followed was an ugly and protracted legal battle that kept Trent Rezner from recording anything under his name or as Nine Inch Nails."

xref.title: Secret Recording as 1000 Homo DJs
xref.body: During his contract dispute with TVT Records, Trent Reznor secretly recorded vocals on a cover of Black Sabbath's "Supernaut" for the Ministry spin-off band 1000 Homo DJs. There is a dispute whether his vocals actually appear on most versions; only versions specifically labeled "Trent Rezner Vocal Version" feature his voice, otherwise it's Al Jourgensen's voice with distortion. "The result was that Trent had to record secretly and under fake names. One such recording was a ministry spin-off band called 1000 homo DJs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Side Project 1000 Homo DJs
xref.body: Ministry's Al Jourgensen initiated a side project called 1000 Homo DJs to release some of Ministry's outtakes. This project utilized fake names for all contributing members, including Jourgensen (Lux/Buck Satan), his songwriting partner Paul Barker (Pan/Officer Aggro), and drummer William Rieflin (We Willy Riefer), and even featured uncredited vocals from Trent Reznor. "He started a goofy side project called 1000 Home Old DJs as a way of releasing some ministry outtakes while keeping things separate from his main band."

xref.title: Sympathy for Trent Reznor
xref.body: Al Jourgensen was very sympathetic to Trent Reznor's contract situation with TVT Records, which led to their collaboration on the 1000 Homo DJs project. "Al Jorrenson was very sympathetic to Trent's situation."
